title: Obligation IR v1
description: The canonical, language-agnostic shape of a compiled obligation. This is the source of truth both apps/core (Java) and apps/brain (Python) validate against -- see SPEC.md for the full rationale behind every field and every deliberate omission. Scope: the compiler-produced IR only (what the extraction pipeline emits). Obligation *lifecycle* fields owned by Phase 5's domain model (status, risk_score, due_at, owner_user_id, version, deleted_at, binding_strength) are deliberately out of scope for this schema -- see SPEC.md section 11.

grammar_version.description: Semver of the grammar this IR instance was compiled under. A grammar bump triggers a recompile job over affected obligations (blueprint SS6.2) -- IR is never silently reinterpreted under a new grammar version.

action.description: A verb from the closed action taxonomy (~40 verbs per blueprint SS6.2, e.g. NOTIFY, DELIVER, PAY, DELETE, RETAIN, MAINTAIN, INDEMNIFY, REPORT, PROVIDE, CURE). The full ~40-verb list is an explicit, tracked open item -- see SPEC.md section 12 -- NOT enumerated as a closed schema enum yet. Only the lexical shape (upper-snake-case) is validated here.

temporal.description: Present-but-nullable, matching the persisted `temporal jsonb` column: the grammar's `temporal?` slot is optional (e.g. MUST_NOT obligations often carry none at all), so the key is always present and is JSON null when no temporal constraint was extracted.

conditions.description: Zero or more IF clauses (blueprint's `condition*`). Deliberately no sibling `exceptions` field -- see SPEC.md section 6. additionalProperties:false at the top level means a payload carrying an `exceptions` key fails validation outright, in both runtimes, rather than silently passing through.

confidence.description: Extraction confidence, matching the `obligations.confidence` CHECK (BETWEEN 0 AND 1).

underspecified.description: True if the typechecker could not fully resolve one or more fields (missing unit, missing anchor, unresolved party, undefined trigger, missing jurisdiction). Underspecified obligations are stored and surfaced, never discarded -- blueprint SS6.2's own design principle: the checker's failures are product features.

missing_fields.description: Named paths of fields the typechecker could not resolve (e.g. "temporal.unit", "obligor"). The exact path-naming convention is a typechecker-design detail for the next checkpoint, not frozen by this spec -- examples in this package use a plausible convention illustratively.

Modality.description: Frozen at exactly these four per blueprint SS21's risk mitigation. Never add a fifth without a grammar_version bump.

PartyRef.description: A reference to an obligor or obligee. The parser only ever produces UNRESOLVED (the alias exactly as it appeared in source text); RESOLVED is written only by the typechecker's symbol-resolution stage (not designed by this checkpoint) once the alias is matched against the org's parties/aliases table.

class.description: The object's class (e.g. "customer_personal_data", "goods", "software"), used by the verifier's conflict-candidate-set matching (blueprint SS6.7). Open vocabulary for v1, same tracked-open-item footing as the action taxonomy -- see SPEC.md section 12.

raw_text.description: The literal object phrase as it appeared in source text, preserved for traceability even after `class` is assigned.

unit.description: bd = business days, requiring a jurisdiction to resolve a calendar (type rule 6, SS6.2) -- else UNDERSPECIFIED[missing:jurisdiction].

DateRef.description: An absolute date, either resolved to a concrete calendar date or an unresolved reference to a defined term/constant (e.g. "the Delivery Date") awaiting typechecker resolution against the document's effective_date and defined terms.

TriggerRef.description: An event or defined-term reference an obligation's timing depends on. RESOLVED distinguishes a declared event type from a defined term (type rule 4, SS6.2: 'trigger must be a declared event type or a defined term in the document -> else UNDEFINED_TRIGGER').

Temporal.description: Frozen at exactly these five forms (blueprint SS21's risk mitigation, with AFTER/BEFORE merged into one directional RELATIVE_TO_TRIGGER form per this checkpoint's own resolution of a real discrepancy between SS6.2's six-alternative grammar sketch and SS21's stated count of five -- see SPEC.md section 3). A genuinely compound expression (e.g. EVERY + DURING together) cannot be represented by any single variant here -- see examples/not-supported/every-during-composition.json.

Predicate.description: Boolean-combinable atoms (blueprint's `predicate := <atom> | predicate (AND|OR) predicate | NOT predicate`). This recursion is ordinary boolean logic within a single IF clause -- distinct from, and unaffected by, the 'no nested exceptions' decision in section 6, which excludes the UNLESS construct entirely, not boolean recursion within a condition's own predicate.

SourceRef.description: The span-grounding citation (Standing Principle 4: extraction output must cite a verbatim source span). NOT NULL on the persisted obligations row -- every IR instance must carry one. char_end > char_start is enforced by the database CHECK constraint and by application-level validation, not expressible in vanilla JSON Schema (no cross-field comparison without vendor extensions).
